Online gaming is no longer limited to playing a game through a browser or downloading an app. Players now have access to multiplayer platforms, mobile games, subscription services, and online casinos, each offering different ways to play and interact. In particular, online casinos have expanded their gaming libraries, offering users a plethora of table games and online slots, as well as live dealer sessions and casino originals. Payment methods on these platforms have also changed. Bank cards and digital wallets remain widely used, but cryptocurrency has become another option for online services that support digital asset payments.

Bitcoin, Ethereum, and stablecoins such as USDT are now accepted by a number of online casino operators, allowing players to use digital assets for deposits and, depending on the platform, withdrawals. For players interested in digital currency gaming, BetUS Casino offers an online destination to explore and play casino games with crypto. Cryptocurrency in this space also raises practical questions about how transactions are processed, which platforms support which assets, and what players should consider before choosing an online casino.

Better internet, mobile tech, and cloud services have changed how online gaming works. Faster connections make real-time multiplayer games easier to play, and cloud services help platforms update games, manage accounts, and let people play on different devices. Now, games can get new content and features without players needing to download a whole new version. Buying digital content is also common on many platforms. These changes have greatly influenced a player’s expectations, especially around easy access and account management.

Online casinos have grown with these changes. Many now offer hundreds or even thousands of games, including slots, table games, and live dealer options, all available on desktop and mobile. Operators also handle digital services like player accounts, game purchases, deposits, and withdrawals. This has created an online space where playing games and paying for them are closely linked.

Cryptocurrency is becoming more common for online payments, giving platforms another way to accept money from users who already have digital assets. Unlike card payments, which go through banks and payment networks, crypto payments move assets directly between blockchain addresses. The kind of cryptocurrency matters too. Bitcoin and Ethereum are well known, but their prices can change quickly, which might affect how much a deposit is worth if the funds stay in those assets. Stablecoins like USDT are different because they are meant to keep a value close to the US dollar. This makes them helpful for people who want to pay digitally without as much price risk, though they still have some risks of their own.

Making a crypto deposit involves more than simply entering a payment amount. The platform or its payment provider supplies a wallet address and specifies which blockchain network to use. Users need to follow these instructions carefully, as assets such as USDT are available across multiple networks that may not be compatible with one another. Once funds are sent, the transaction is verified and recorded on the relevant blockchain. The receiving platform may require a set number of network confirmations before crediting the account. Transaction fees and processing times also vary depending on the asset, network activity, and the platform’s own deposit procedures.

Cryptocurrency and online casinos are connected in more ways than just adding Bitcoin or USDT as payment options. Some casinos are built specifically for users with digital assets, so their account balances, deposits, and withdrawals are set up for crypto transactions. Others add crypto tokens to their existing payment systems, which already include bank cards and digital wallets. For players, these differences can change how casinos manage funds and which currencies are available. Also, not every casino treats crypto the same way. Some may let you deposit with a certain cryptocurrency but not withdraw with it.

Online casino users now have more ways to pay, but other things still set casinos apart. They still compete on the games they offer, the software they use, mobile access, withdrawal rules, and customer support. Accepting several cryptocurrencies might attract people who use digital assets, but that doesn’t tell potential players much about the casino’s overall quality. Payment terms, game selection, and withdrawal conditions are still important.

As more online casinos start accepting cryptocurrency, players now have more choices than ever. But payment methods are just one factor to think about. The selection of games can be very different from one casino to another. Most well-known casinos have slots, table games, and live dealer options, but the number of games and the companies that make them can vary. Some casinos even create their own games or offer exclusive titles you won’t find elsewhere. For example, BetUS Casino has over 700 games with more games in the pipeline awaiting their launch, so players have plenty to try.

Casinos also use promotions to bring in new players, offering things like deposit bonuses, free bets, and other rewards. BetUS, for example, has several types of bonuses. One is a 150% Sportsbook bonus, which offers up to $750 across a player’s first three deposits, with a $50 minimum deposit and a 10x rollover requirement in sports. These offers can look appealing, but the attached conditions matter as much as the advertised rewards. Players should also consider licensing, account security, withdrawal policies, and customer support when comparing platforms. Casino ratings and independent reviews can help narrow options, but players should consider them alongside these practical details rather than treating them as a guarantee of quality.

Crypto payments let players control how they move their money, but it also places greater responsibility on the person making the transaction. Anyone using a personal wallet should protect their private keys and recovery phrases, as losing access to them can mean losing access to their funds. It is equally important to check the receiving address and blockchain network before confirming a transfer. Crypto transactions generally cannot be reversed once confirmed, so sending funds to an incorrect address or through an unsupported network can make recovery difficult or impossible. Players should also account for network fees, which can change with demand, and confirmation times, which may affect when a casino credits a deposit or processes a withdrawal.

It’s just as important to check out the casino itself. Just because a casino accepts Bitcoin, Ethereum, or USDT doesn’t mean it’s licensed or allowed to operate everywhere. Players should check which regulatory authority issued its licence, whether that licence covers online gambling, and whether the operator is permitted to accept customers from their jurisdiction. They should also understand the platform’s withdrawal procedures, including any limits, verification requirements, processing conditions, or restrictions on cryptocurrency withdrawals, before depositing funds.

Its services include betting odds, sports analysis, and customer support, with a focus on providing users with access to wagering opportunities across different categories.

Crypto gaming, sometimes called Web3 or blockchain gaming, means playing online games or using entertainment platforms that use cryptocurrencies or blockchain technology. This includes online casino games that accept digital currencies and games where players can own or trade digital items.

Players usually send cryptocurrency from their own wallet or an exchange to the casino’s deposit address. Once the transaction is confirmed on the blockchain, the casino adds the funds to the player’s account. Withdrawing works in much the same way.

Many online casinos accept cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin and Ethereum. Some also support Litecoin and stablecoins such as USDT. Since payment options vary, it’s a good idea to check which coins and networks each casino supports.

Crypto casinos can be safer if they are run by licensed and regulated companies. Players should check for clear licensing details on the site and confirm them with the authority that issued them. It’s also important to keep wallets secure and gamble responsibly.

#5255. Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse Breaks Silence on XRP vs. RLUSD Debate

Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse addressed the ongoing debate over the potential impact of Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin on XRP’s future, asserting that both assets are complementary rather than competitive.

On Nov. 3, Brad Garlinghouse offered his view in response to a comprehensive X post from a notable member of the XRP Ledger community named Vet, who outlined the key differences between the two assets associated with Ripple.

“Well said, Vet. Complementary, not competitive,” the Ripple chief executive tweeted.

The brief statement comes amid pushback as some XRP holders are increasingly concerned that Ripple’s aggressive foray into the stablecoin market may negatively impact demand for XRP in the future.

As part of his viral post, Vet explained that the key difference between the two assets revolves around the purposes they serve on the XRP Ledger.

“RLUSD is optional. XRP isn’t,” the commentator explained.

As the XRP Ledger’s native currency, XRP is essential for the core functions of the network. First, every account must have an XRP reserve. Second, transaction fees are paid in XRP.

RLUSD, on the other hand, is a dollar-denominated stablecoin issued by Ripple's regulated stablecoin business. The key difference is that, unlike XRP, the value of RLUSD is supposed to remain stable at roughly $1.

Another key difference lies in control over the assets.

Ripple has the ability to freeze RLUSD under certain conditions, for example, to meet legal obligations. There is no central entity that can freeze XRP, the native cryptocurrency, on the ledger.

According to Vet, another key advantage of XRP is its privileged status on the XRP Ledger's DEX.

The XRP Ledger has an automatic bridging function. In this way, if it makes sense to trade between currencies through XRP for a better exchange rate, trades can be automatically routed through XRP.

This is why XRP is so valuable for liquidity providers and market makers as an intermediary asset.

On the other hand, RLUSD would be much more suitable in cases where price stability is important, for example, for payroll, invoicing, corporate payments, etc.

At the same time, some XRP investors are worried that one day RLUSD may effectively replace XRP for some payment use cases.

The crucial question is this: If you can send a dollar-denominated stablecoin directly, why would you need to use an intermediary like XRP?

It’s also worth noting that RLUSD isn’t exclusive to the XRP Ledger. In fact, RLUSD also works on Ethereum and other supported blockchains. So increasing demand for RLUSD doesn’t necessarily lead to more use of the XRP Ledger.

And even if we’re seeing more RLUSD transactions on the XRP Ledger, this doesn’t automatically mean that increased demand for XRP to pay transaction fees necessarily guarantees a significant price surge for the cryptocurrency.

It’s not the first time Garlinghouse has been forced to comment on Ripple's changing priorities.

During Ripple’s Swell 2026 conference in New York on Oct. 28, Ripple’s CEO directly addressed rumors that Ripple is becoming increasingly focused on RLUSD rather than XRP.

“We will never give up on XRP,” Garlinghouse said.

Until ADA makes higher lows and reclaims its major moving averages, any move up looks more like a short bounce than a proper bullish reversal.

Home » Ripple (XRP) » Ripple Treasury Links To SWIFT With XRP-Linked Hook

SWIFT’s ISO 20022 gold standard covers a lot of territory in terms of Ripple-linked banking systems.

A former SWIFT standards veteran with more than 27 years at the messaging network says ISO 20022 gives banks a practical way to handle digital assets without rebuilding their back offices.

At the same time, Ripple Treasury’s documented partnerships with SWIFT keep XRP in the conversation as traditional and blockchain rails continue to overlap.

Tom Alaerts, who spent the bulk of his career working on the standards that underpin global payments, has pushed back on the idea that blockchain will simply replace SWIFT.

In a recent conversation with SMQKE, the popular blockchain researcher, he argued that decades of trust, security, neutrality & governance still make the cooperative hard to displace.

My full conversation with Tom Alaerts, who spent over 27 years at SWIFT working on the standards the global payment system runs on.😶‍🌫️Every technical difficulty has been cut out. What is left in this video below is the complete conversation from start to finish, for anyone who… pic.twitter.com/WAFSDof848

What has changed, he said, is the standard itself. Updates around 2022 and 2023 made it easier to represent digital token identifiers, blockchain addresses & higher numerical precision inside the securities messages banks already use.

That means institutions can process tokenized assets through existing systems rather than standing up entirely new infrastructure.

SWIFT’s Tom Alaerts noted that ISO-compliant networks and fintechs face fewer hurdles when banks and central-bank systems evaluate them.

Because they already use terminology and data structures familiar to traditional finance, security reviews, resilience testing, and regulatory checks become less friction-heavy.

He fundamentally expects a hybrid environment in which traditional messaging and blockchain settlement coexist rather than one displacing the other.

🚨A former SWIFT expert with 27 YEARS of experience says ISO 20022 makes it EASIER for $XRP to integrate with GLOBAL BANKING. pic.twitter.com/VijDbUdsAS

For digital assets, SWIFT networks that already map cleanly to ISO 20022, that hybrid path is shorter.

Another SWIFT – Ripple related discussion has focused on Ripple Treasury, the platform that emerged after Ripple’s acquisition of GTreasury. Materials highlight strategic partnerships with leading banks, SWIFT, Refinitiv & other providers to support end-to-end corporate treasury workflows.

The platform sits inside SWIFT’s Certified Partner Program and offers connectivity options such as Alliance Lite2 along with tools for IBAN and ABA lookups. It also lets corporate users manage both traditional fiat balances and digital assets including XRP and RLUSD in one place.

The connection is at the treasury-platform level rather than a direct pipe from the XRP Ledger into SWIFT messaging, but it still places XRP inside a workflow that already touches the network banks rely on daily.

Taken together, the two threads point to the same practical outcome: banks do not need to abandon existing rails to experiment with digital assets.

SWIFT’s ISO 20022 gold standard supplies a shared language, while platforms such as Ripple Treasury supply the operational layer that can sit alongside those rails. SWIFT remains central because of the trust and governance already built around it.

Networks and assets that align with the standard, and that appear inside the tools corporate treasurers already use, are simply better positioned as the two systems continue to converge.

#5252. Elon Musk Mocks Sam Altman Over Claim Home PCs Are Wasting RAM

Elon Musk Mocks Sam Altman Over Claim Home PCs Are Wasting RAM

Elon Musk has mocked OpenAI CEO Sam Altman for arguing that the world's limited supply of computer memory would be better used in AI data centers than in people's home computers.

Altman made the comments in an interview with the YouTube channel Cheeky Pint, while discussing the shortages of memory and other components caused by the AI boom.

"A lot of people want local inference, and somehow they assume that the problem is solved now because we're going to have open-source models," Altman said, referring to running AI models on a user's own hardware. "But from like a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5% of the time."

"You want maximum utilization in a cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply-constrained environment," he added. "And somehow, many people's intuition is the opposite of that."

Musk responded on X on Sunday with a meme showing Hans Landa, the Nazi officer played by Christoph Waltz in the film Inglourious Basterds, captioned: "You are withholding DRAM from the cloud, are you not?" "The people deserve to have their RAM too!" Musk wrote alongside the image.

The people deserve to have their RAM too! pic.twitter.com/q6dwauALw4

In the interview, Altman blamed the shortage partly on memory makers' caution. For years, a DRAM producer "would invest $20 billion of CapEx to make $19 billion," he said, and companies that nearly went bankrupt building too many factories in past cycles have been slow to expand, even as they now stand to generate huge profits.

Altman said he would like to see prices for energy, chips and the rest of the supply chain fall. "If it doesn't go down, I'll be very sad," he said, adding that for prices to fall, supply needs to grow.

The jab is the latest in a long-running feud between the two men, who co-founded OpenAI with others in 2015 before Musk left in 2018.

Musk sued OpenAI and Altman in 2024, accusing them of abandoning the organization's founding nonprofit mission. In May, a federal jury in California rejected the $150 billion lawsuit, finding OpenAI, Altman and president Greg Brockman not liable on all claims. OpenAI's lawyers had argued that the suit was motivated in part by competition, after Musk launched rival AI company xAI in 2023.

#5250. Binance relied on AI to fight fraud before hackers exploited internal tool in $6 billion theft

Attackers exploited an internal AI system to reach wallet engineers, prompting the exchange to seek security partnerships with leading AI companies.

Hackers exploited Binance's internal artificial intelligence tools to compromise engineers before stealing $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency, the exchange disclosed.

In its Nov. 3 security report, Binance said attackers used a compromised employee computer and an internal AI tool on Oct. 20 to take control of two engineers responsible for its wallet infrastructure.

The attackers subsequently obtained access to a container deployment permission token, which helped them penetrate the exchange's wallet-signing operations on Oct. 29 and initiate unauthorized transactions across several blockchain networks.

The disclosure puts AI at the center of one of the largest cryptocurrency thefts on record, adding to concerns about how increasingly connected AI systems can introduce new vulnerabilities into corporate infrastructure.

Binance's investigation does not establish that an AI model autonomously planned or executed the theft. Rather, the attackers exploited an internal AI tool as part of a broader campaign involving stolen credentials, compromised developer software, and social engineering.

In June, a Binance engineer downloaded a tampered software installer while attempting to install a popular AI coding tool. Binance detected the suspicious activity, replaced the device and rotated associated credentials, although information about the employee and colleagues had already been exposed.

In September, another engineer fell victim to a fake recruitment operation involving staged job interviews and a malicious coding assignment. The malware compromised the employee's computer and gave the attackers access, which they later used to move deeper into Binance's systems.

The FBI has attributed the broader attack to North Korea, whose hacking operations have increasingly targeted software developers and cryptocurrency businesses.

The Binance incident follows months of warnings from cybersecurity researchers that artificial intelligence is expanding both hackers' capabilities and the systems available for exploitation.

In February, Google's Mandiant reported that North Korean hackers targeting the cryptocurrency industry had incorporated AI-assisted techniques into their operations.

The researchers documented an intrusion involving a fake video conference, malicious software, and a suspected AI-generated video impersonating a corporate executive. They could not independently confirm the deepfake in that particular incident but identified the group's use of AI tools for reconnaissance and social engineering.

By September, Google's Threat Intelligence Group reported that attackers were moving beyond using AI to generate malicious content toward automated operations that could execute multiple stages of an intrusion.

In one case, hackers compromised a cloud resource and organized an AI-assisted mass credential-harvesting campaign in less than six hours. Google also identified attackers attempting to manipulate AI coding assistants and security scanners during software supply-chain compromises.

The findings closely resemble one aspect of the Binance breach: developers and the AI-powered tools they depend on are becoming targets attackers use to reach sensitive systems.

Separately, AI developer Anthropic disclosed in September that criminals and suspected state-sponsored operators had used its Claude models to conduct reconnaissance, develop exploitation tools, and automate data theft.

Some operations involved AI agents carrying out multiple stages of an attack with limited human supervision, reducing the technical expertise and manpower traditionally required.

The exchange is now seeking support from the same industry whose technologies were featured in the attack.

Binance said it is working to establish a security research fund and develop targeted initiatives with leading AI companies, blockchain industry participants and cybersecurity firms.

The proposed collaboration will focus on strengthening AI security in blockchain environments, although the exchange has not disclosed the fund's proposed size, participating companies or launch date.

It also plans to expand spending on AI-enabled threat detection, endpoint protection, developer-environment security and behavioral anomaly monitoring.

The exchange said it has already rebuilt the affected internal AI tool and wallet infrastructure, replaced compromised employee devices and strengthened access controls.

Binance has also commissioned an independent cybersecurity review to validate its investigation and identify additional safeguards.

The company said approximately $2.85 billion of the $6.34 billion in affected digital assets has been frozen or intercepted, while 98% of impacted token assets had been replenished as of Oct. 31.

The independent review has yet to establish the full extent of the weaknesses that allowed attackers to exploit the exchange's internal AI environment. Its findings will inform the security changes Binance plans to implement as it develops the proposed industry fund.

#5249. Binance Hacker Continues Aggressive Bitcoin Buying Spree

The hacker behind the monumental Binance attack is still buying up more Bitcoin (BTC).

As per the latest blockchain analytics data from Lookonchain dated Nov. 4, the hacker continues to exchange SOL for Bitcoin, moving the stolen assets across several crypto wallets.

The blockchain tracker added that the hacker is using the following multi-step process to exchange the stolen crypto for Bitcoin.

The hacker’s complicated scheme involves splitting his SOL assets among different wallets before selling the SOL for USDC, transferring the USDC from Solana to Ethereum, buying ETH using the USDC and finally exchanging the newly bought ETH for BTC using THORChain, a decentralized cross-chain liquidity protocol.

This long and complicated cross-chain transaction process allows the hacker to easily transfer his funds between different blockchain networks. It also makes it harder to trace the stolen assets.

This in not the first time that the hacker has been buying Bitcoin with the stolen funds. In fact, he had earlier been seen making transactions to buy Bitcoin using tens of millions of dollars’ worth of stolen SOL.

As per Lookonchain’s data dated Nov. 1, the hacker behind the Binance hack was trying to convert approximately 970,522 SOL, worth roughly $95.9 million at the time of writing, into Bitcoin.

The hacker was even seen making a transaction involving 486,970 SOL (approximately $46.4M) in just one hour.

However, during these transactions, the hacker used a different service called Relay Protocol, which also allows cross-chain crypto transfers.

From the recent blockchain data, it looks like the hacker is still focused on Bitcoin. He’s also using several decentralized services to exchange the stolen crypto.

The latest official update from Binance shows that the massive security breach has affected crypto assets worth around $6.34 billion.

As per the update, the exchange says that it has frozen/intercepted about $2.85 billion worth of stolen cryptocurrency as of Nov. 3.

According to US federal authorities, the attack was conducted by a North Korean state-sponsored hacker group called TraderTraitor.

The FBI is also asking various decentralized crypto services like THORChain to prevent funds linked to the attack from moving around.

Even with all these efforts, the latest on-chain data shows that the hacker is still moving stolen funds across different networks.

#5248. US Democrats Sweep Midterms: Bitcoin Back to $78K, Stock Market Wobbles

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » US Democrats Sweep Midterms: Bitcoin Back to $78K, Stock Market Wobbles

Bitcoin recovered toward $78,000 after Democrats won control, while Asian stocks and the dollar came under pressure.

A historic Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections triggered initial stock market tremors across Asia and Wall Street tech shares. However, Bitcoin quickly reversed early losses, bouncing from $75,700 back toward $78,000 despite ongoing ETF outflows.

The results arrived during Asian trading hours on November 4. AI-related shares fell across the region, Treasury yields dipped, and the dollar weakened. US stock futures dropped sharply before paring losses.

Japan’s Nikkei index fell 2,543 points to 60,538.67, breaking below its 200-day moving average. A stronger yen weighed on exporters and semiconductor stocks, while Nintendo and Fast Retailing bucked the decline.

On Election Day, November 3, Wall Street ended a losing streak on a chip rally. The S&P 500 rose 0.36% to 7,568.92, and the Nasdaq Composite gained 0.83% to 25,372.01. The Dow fell 0.38% to 51,786.72 after Apple warned that higher memory costs could squeeze margins.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 2.63%. Nvidia rose 2.29%, lifting its market value back above $5 trillion, and AMD climbed 3.65%. After the close, AMD reported 45% year-over-year growth in third-quarter revenue and forecast fourth-quarter revenue of about $17 billion, versus analyst expectations of $16.2 billion.

Bitcoin price briefly hit a seven-week low near $75,700 before recovering toward $78,000 on November 4. The rebound followed a broader reassessment of the political implications of Democrats taking control of Congress after US voters delivered a strong rebuke to Donald Trump’s policies.

Ethereum gained around 2.6% to $2,319, and Solana climbed 1.6% to $93.70.

However, institutional demand remained a concern. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $115.56 million in net outflows on November 3, marking their third consecutive day of withdrawals, according to SoSoValue data.

Analysts Expect Volatility, Not a Policy Overhaul

The historic Democratic victory followed growing voter discontent over Trump’s unilateral decisions, tariffs, and rising oil prices driven by the war in Iran. Analysts expect short-term volatility as investors assess gridlock, tighter regulation, and reduced fiscal stimulus.

Tech and AI stocks could face pressure from scrutiny of Big Tech and data-centre spending, and crypto may face regulatory uncertainty.

However, analysts caution against overreacting to the election outcome. Trump keeps his veto power and significant influence over trade, tariffs and foreign policy, limiting the scope for major policy changes. Lower Treasury yields could also provide support for equities, potentially easing the initial sell-off.

Overall, analysts expect volatility rather than a fundamental shift in the market outlook, with corporate earnings, economic growth, and interest rates likely to remain the key drivers of the stock market.

#5247. Coinbase XRP looked cheap on Nov. 2 despite identical market value

At the Nov. 2 close, an independent comparison narrows XRP’s Coinbase discount from 0.168% to 0.006% after converting USDT into dollars.

XRP’s apparent Coinbase discount at the Nov. 2 close shrinks from about 0.168% to 0.006% when Binance’s Tether (USDT) quote is converted into dollars. The independent exchange-price comparison separates the quote-currency effect from the remaining difference in XRP prices.

The user Arab Chain on CryptoQuant reported an approximately -0.16% XRP Coinbase Premium Index reading on Nov. 2, describing it as an eight-month low and interpreting it as relatively weaker Coinbase demand.

The post also cautioned that the index alone was not definitive evidence of continued downside pressure.

The completed Nov. 2 candles put Coinbase XRP/USD at $1.2481, Binance XRP/USDT at 1.2502 USDT and Coinbase USDT/USD at $0.99838.

The adjustment multiplies Binance’s XRP price by USDT’s dollar price, then compares Coinbase against that converted figure. Expressed as a percentage, the formula is:

100 × [Coinbase XRP/USD ÷ (Binance XRP/USDT × USDT/USD) − 1].

This uses Coinbase’s USDT/USD market as the conversion reference. It is a venue price, rather than a universal redemption rate or evidence about why USDT traded below one dollar.

At the November 2 close, the gap shrinks after converting USDT into dollars. October 31 shows why the adjustment does not always leave near parity.

November 2, 2026 UTC close: raw -0.168%; dollar-adjusted -0.006%. The remaining dollar-price gap is close to zero.

October 31, 2026 UTC close: raw -0.200%; dollar-adjusted -0.078%. A residual discount remains after conversion.

Normalize the quote currency first. Then ask whether a remaining venue-price discount persists.

Closing trades are asynchronous, not executable quotes. Coinbase USDT/USD is a venue reference. Fees, spreads and rounding matter. This does not reproduce CryptoQuant’s proprietary index or identify selling counterparties.

The raw percentage compares Coinbase’s dollar close directly with Binance’s USDT close. The adjusted percentage first multiplies Binance’s close by Coinbase USDT/USD, then divides Coinbase XRP/USD by that product, subtracts one and multiplies by 100. Completed UTC days only. Labels and bars use three-decimal percentages on a shared scale from minus 0.25 percent to zero.

Closing trades are asynchronous, not executable quotes. Coinbase USDT/USD is a venue reference. Fees, spreads and rounding matter. This does not reproduce CryptoQuant’s proprietary index or identify selling counterparties.

Across all seven completed UTC daily observations, the adjustment narrowed the discount, but did not eliminate it every day:

Negative values mean Coinbase was cheaper, while positive values mean it was more expensive. Figures are rounded to three decimal places from the three exchange datasets.

Oct. 30 and 31 adjusted discounts remained about 0.066% and 0.078%, respectively, and the Nov. 2 finding supports checking the currency conversion.

A separate check used 60 matched one-minute buckets from Nov. 2, 12:00-12:59 UTC, combining Coinbase XRP/USD, Binance XRP/USDT and Coinbase USDT/USD. Its median raw gap was about -0.128%, and the median dollar-adjusted gap was approximately +0.006%.

XRP was near $1.28 on Nov. 3. Around 13:15 UTC, Coinbase’s ticker reported a $1.276 last trade, above its $1.2481 Nov. 2 close, while Binance’s rolling ticker showed 1.2780 USDT.

A relative-demand warning would be more persuasive if a discount persisted after currency conversion alongside comparatively heavier seller-initiated XRP trading over equivalent windows.

The measurement stops short of an executable arbitrage test. Coinbase defines candle closes as the last trade within each bucket, while Binance’s candles use matching time intervals. Rounding, bid-ask spreads, fees, and differences between venues are important when a residual gap is this small.

An August 2025 XRP liquidity study exposed a similar disconnect: XRP prices remained closely aligned across Binance and Coinbase even as trading activity was concentrated in different quote currencies.

Price consistency does not guarantee equally accessible liquidity, and traders may see nearly identical quotes but face substantially different execution costs and slippage, particularly during periods of market stress.

On Nov. 2’s closing observations, the unadjusted gap by itself substantially overstates the remaining dollar-price difference.

The current decline in XRP's market value has not led to loss-taking by large stakeholders — on the contrary, a phase of aggressive accumulation has unfolded in the market. According to data from the analytical platform Santiment, an absolute record for the current year has been set on the XRP Ledger network: 2,147 wallets now hold a balance of 1 million tokens or more.

The main inflow of capital came during the price correction period, when the asset's market price dropped to the $1.27 mark.

The main activity of large capital unfolded at the end of October. The dynamics with which investors are forming large positions points to a rigid strategic calculation: over the past ten days, 28 new addresses have attained millionaire status, and 18 of them were opened during the final three days of the reporting period.

Unlike speculative capital oriented toward quick profit, large holders traditionally use phases of price weakness for buying. The growth in the number of millionaires at such a moment confirms that large balances are being systematically increased rather than liquidated.

Such divergences between a falling chart and an inflow of institutional capital often precede the formation of a long-term market bottom.

Is this surge a signal that the price has found a bottom? Analysts identify three clear price thresholds that will give a precise answer to this question in the coming days:

• The $1.20 – $1.25 zone (Foundation): A critical support line and the main indicator of a potential bottom. If the price holds in this range and the number of millionaire wallets remains above 2,140, the long-term growth scenario will remain in force.

• The $1.30 milestone (Psychology): A local resistance level, a return above which is necessary to confirm a reversal and restore optimism in the mass market.

• The $1.40 level (Confirmation): Consolidation of the price above this mark amid a continuing inflow of large holders will prove that the bottom has been definitively passed and that capital is ready to drive the asset toward new highs.

Thus, the sustainability of XRP's current bullish setup depends directly on the ability of large capital to hold key support levels during the coming market movements.

#5243. Evernorth Filing To Unlock 12 Million Shares For Resale

Home » Trendsetter News » Evernorth Filing To Unlock 12 Million Shares For Resale

Evernorth’s resale filing could potentially expand the tradable pool from 7 million to 19 million, analyst Dana Love says.

About 12 million additional Evernorth shares could become eligible for sale once a resale registration takes effect, according to crypto commentator Dana Love.

In a new video examining the XRP treasury company’s filings, Love argues that this potential supply matters more than the much larger registration headline & could reshape trading in a stock with a relatively small float.

XRPN fell from an opening price of $14.19 to $11.74 by early afternoon in the session discussed, a decline of roughly 17%. Love noted that the selloff followed the filing but stopped short of calling it the cause: “It’s a data point, not a verdict.”

The filing registers 73.7 million shares for resale across Evernorth’s capital structure. That does not mean all those shares are immediately available to sell.

Love’s calculation puts the existing tradable pool at roughly 7 million shares. Another approximately 12 million Class A shares could become eligible once the SEC declares the registration effective, potentially bringing that pool to about 19 million.

SBI Holdings owns 9.4 million Class A shares, or 36.1% of that class, according to the filing figures cited in the video. It is not among the holders subject to the six-month lockup ending around April 9; Ripple, the Arrington fund and the Larson trust are.

Eligibility is not intent. Love describes SBI’s investment as strategic and estimates that its main-round holdings were substantially underwater at the prices discussed.

The video also challenges share counts that exclude Evernorth’s other equity interests. Including Class A shares, Class C shares and exchangeable units, Love arrives at approximately 80.4 million shares against 473.3 million XRP – about 5.88 XRP per share.

At the video’s cited XRP price near $1.25, that represents roughly $7.35 in XRP per share. XRPN’s $11.74 price therefore still reflected a premium of about 60% to that backing.

Dana Love, PhD says the subscription agreements target registration effectiveness within 75 days of the October 9 closing, or December 23, with an extension possible if the SEC reviews the filing. That contractual timetable is not an SEC approval date.

Investors have two separate developments to watch: whether registered holders actually sell, and whether Evernorth uses its equity financing facility above XRP backing value to increase XRP per share.

More eligible stock could pressure the premium; issuing stock at a premium could improve the underlying XRP allocation.

#5242. Nvidia and Nike Lead Biggest Wave Yet of Tokenized Stock Objections

Nvidia and Nike Lead Biggest Wave Yet of Tokenized Stock Objections

Even Nvidia doesn’t want its shares on OKX and ICE’s planned tokenized stock venue.

The chipmaker is among 12 new companies listed as objecting issuers in an updated notice from OKXICE TSV dated Friday. The others are Costco, Nike, Micron, CrowdStrike, Palo Alto Networks, Reddit, Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Corning, Bloom Energy, IREN, and USA Rare Earth. The additions bring the total to 50 companies.

It’s the largest single batch yet. The list stood at 38 in the venue’s Oct. 28 notice, when Walmart and Eli Lilly joined, and at nine when the first objectors appeared on Oct. 15. It has more than quintupled since.

The newcomers span chips, cybersecurity, retail, and energy. Nvidia, Micron, and Corning join hardware peers such as AMD, Intel, and Broadcom, while CrowdStrike and Palo Alto Networks bring cybersecurity heavyweights to the list. IREN, a Bitcoin miner that has expanded into AI cloud computing, adds a name from the crypto industry itself.

Under the SEC’s innovation exemption, which the agency unveiled in September after the Clarity Act stalled in the Senate, a venue must notify a company before offering a version of its shares tokenized by an unaffiliated third party. If the company objects in writing within 30 days, the venue can’t make that stock available for trading, according to the SEC’s order. The objection applies only to that venue.

OKXICE TSV, a 50-50 joint venture between NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange and OKX’s U.S. holding company, plans to let approved users trade tokenized U.S. stocks around the clock. Trades would run through permissioned Uniswap v4 pools on OKX’s XLayer blockchain, paired with stablecoins such as USDC.

None of the objecting companies have explained their decisions, but Nasdaq offered one possible rationale when it opted its own shares out of the exemption.

A spokesperson told The Wall Street Journal that Nasdaq doesn’t want its stock trading on a venue that doesn’t show the best prices in real time or report trades to the consolidated tape.

Further, Crypto in America reported that Nasdaq may be playing a role behind the scenes in encouraging companies to opt out of the OKX-ICE venture. “Our Nasdaq rep had reached out to us regarding OKX listing, suggesting we should object and that they would hold a call to discuss why,” an executive at a Nasdaq-listed company told the publication. “Nasdaq is definitely partly behind this,” the exec reportedly said.

OKXICE’s notice acknowledges it isn’t subject to Regulation NMS, the rules designed to ensure investors get the best displayed prices. It also warns that broker-dealers face unsettled questions about trade reporting and best execution on the venue.

Some of the market’s biggest names, including Apple, Tesla and Amazon, still haven’t appeared on the list.

#5241. Binance stopped 57 North Korean cyber threats but fell for a fake job interview

The exchange's defenses thwarted dozens of suspected attacks before hackers used a staged recruitment process to infiltrate its wallet systems.

Binance said it thwarted 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threats in 2026, yet a fake interview compromised one of its engineers.

The disclosure, in the exchange's Nov. 3 security report, reveals how attackers used a recruitment scam involving staged interviews, fabricated identities, and malicious software to access systems involved in the $6.34 billion cryptocurrency theft on Oct. 29.

“Throughout 2026, Binance's security team detected and prevented 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threat cases. These attempts reflect the persistent threat posed by state-sponsored actors targeting the cryptocurrency industry. The techniques include fraudulent job interviews, malicious software disguised as popular developer tools, compromised software packages and browser extensions, fake video conferencing applications, and social engineering campaigns designed to steal credentials or deploy remote access malware. We intercepted many of them, but the cost of failing to stop even one was severe—and this should never have happened.”

The operation succeeded despite Binance's security team identifying and preventing dozens of suspected North Korean intrusion attempts during the year, including campaigns using fraudulent job interviews and compromised developer tools.

The FBI attributed the theft to North Korea's TraderTraitor operation on Oct. 31, describing an ongoing effort to steal cryptocurrency and launder the proceeds through decentralized finance platforms.

Binance's findings expose a troubling gap between recognizing a persistent threat and preventing its execution.

The campaign's earliest identified stage occurred in June, when a Binance wallet infrastructure engineer downloaded a tampered Homebrew installer while attempting to install a popular AI coding tool.

Binance's security team detected the suspicious software, replaced the device, and rotated related credentials. However, the incident exposed information about the engineer's responsibilities and colleagues.

In September, someone impersonating a project director at a fictitious company approached another software engineer through a legitimate recruitment platform.

An individual posing as a human resources representative conducted a live video interview and shared a social media profile containing personal photographs and videos to establish credibility.

A second interview followed with someone claiming to be the company's chief executive.

Near the end of that conversation, the engineer was instructed to download a coding assignment onto his work computer. The repository contained malware that executed during setup, replacing a legitimate developer-tool component and establishing communication with an attacker-controlled server.

Binance said the previously unknown malware evaded its endpoint security software and concealed traces of the intrusion.

By Oct. 20, the attackers had used the compromised computer and an internal AI tool to gain control over two additional engineers, including the employee targeted in June.

They subsequently obtained a container deployment permission token. Nine days later, the attackers used stolen credentials to deploy a malicious container and reach Binance's wallet-signing infrastructure.

The exchange said the attackers initiated unauthorized transfers outside its normal withdrawal process, draining assets across several blockchain networks.

The tactics closely resemble a North Korean cyber operation that security researchers and US authorities have tracked for years.

In September 2024, the FBI warned that North Korean hackers were using highly personalized employment opportunities, elaborate fictional identities, and prolonged conversations to infiltrate cryptocurrency businesses.

The agency noted that even technically sophisticated employees could be deceived by campaigns tailored to their professional backgrounds.

That playbook remained active throughout 2026.

In June, Kudelski Security researchers documented North Korea's Contagious Interview operation, in which hackers impersonated recruiters on LinkedIn, WhatsApp and Discord before persuading developers to execute malicious code.

By September, Atlassian researchers had identified fake technical assessments hosted on established development platforms, where malicious instructions were hidden within otherwise legitimate-looking software projects.

The similarities raise questions about why Binance's existing threat detection measures failed to identify the successful recruitment campaign.

The exchange has not disclosed how many of the 57 prevented cases involved fake interviews or whether any were directly connected to the group behind the October breach.

Following the attack, Binance said it replaced compromised employee devices, revoked exposed credentials, and rebuilt affected wallet infrastructure. It also strengthened developer-environment protections and expanded AI-based behavioral monitoring.

#5240. 1win Team Secure Direct Qualification for Major Stage 2 After Moscow Cyber Games 2026 Victory

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

1win Team secured guaranteed participation in Stage 2 of the upcoming Counter-Strike 2 Major after winning Moscow Cyber Games 2026. The team defeated HOTU 2-0 in the grand final, claiming the championship title and $98,000 (equivalent to RUB 8 million) in prize money.

In the grand final on November 1, 1win Team delivered a convincing performance across both maps, winning 13-9 on Anubis and 13-11 on Dust2. The victory marks a major milestone for 1win and establishes its revamped CS2 roster among the world’s top teams.

“Winning Moscow Cyber Games means much more to us than just a trophy. We are the roster built from the ground up, and not many people in the industry believed we could reach this level so quickly. But as a team, we put in the work, stayed focused on our goals, and trusted each other throughout our training camps and official matches,” 1win Team captain nafany (Vladislav Gorshkov) commented on the win, mentioning, “Now we’re heading straight to Stage 2 of the Major, and that’s exactly where we want to be. This is only the beginning, and we’re hungry for more.”

The Moscow triumph is the latest in a remarkable rise for 1win Team CS2. The roster has already made headlines on the international stage with its performance at ESL Pro League Season 24, where the team defeated Team Spirit 2-0 in one of the tournament’s biggest upsets. 1win followed up the victory with wins over G2 and Legacy, finishing the group stage with a 3-1 record and securing a playoff berth. The Team Spirit upset also earned the players a $100,000 bonus from the owner of 1win.

What makes 1win Team’s achievements particularly remarkable is the story behind the roster. The organization built an entirely new lineup from scratch, bringing together players looking for a fresh opportunity to revive their careers. In a remarkably short period, the team has transformed from a newly assembled project into an international contender, winning major tournaments and securing a place among the world’s top 12 CS2 teams. The Moscow Cyber Games title brings further opportunities, including invitations to two prestigious Tier 1 events: BLAST Bounty and PGL Cluj-Napoca.

From a completely new roster to victories over Team Spirit and a Moscow Cyber Games championship, 1win Team have quickly established themselves as a force to watch in Counter-Strike 2. With BLAST Bounty, PGL Cluj-Napoca, and Major Stage 2 ahead, the team has another chance to make a major breakthrough.

The current 1win Team Counter-Strike 2 roster joined the organization on August 1, 2026. The lineup features Vladislav “nafany” Gorshkov, Sergey “Ax1Le” Rykhtorov, Andrey “BELCHONOKK” Yasinskiy, Petr “fame” Bolyshev, and Artem “ArtFr0st” Kharitonov, coached by Konstantin “groove” Pikiner. 1win Team is currently developing a dedicated training base for the roster in Serbia, the same location the organization previously used for its Dota 2 bootcamp. Streaming service W.TV serves as the team’s general sponsor.
